About Us
Almost every single thing that you eat, wear, or use (yes, even the screen you’re reading this on) is imported. Freight quite literally moves the world. And we’re helping it move even better.
Freightos (Nasdaq: CRGO) is the global booking and payment platform for the trillion-dollar freight industry. Hundreds of airlines and ocean liners, thousands of freight companies, and over ten thousand importers and exporters use our platform to move goods around the world faster and more efficiently. This matters. Efficient freight ultimately makes things cost a little bit less when you buy them in the store.
As the leading global freight booking platform for a massive industry, we’ve been crushing it with double-digit growth, year after year, supporting well over one million shipments every year.
About the Role
Freightos Group is seeking a dynamic FP&A Analyst experienced in financial planning and analysis. As an integral part of our Finance team, you will significantly contribute to shaping strategic decisions across the company. This role involves ensuring the precision of financial forecasts, delivering insightful analyses, and spearheading process improvements that drive our growth and profitability. If you’re passionate about financial strategy and eager to make a tangible impact in a leading global logistics technology company, we’d love to have you on board.
Responsibilities
Financial Reporting
Conducting comprehensive analyses of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements.
Crafting insightful reports to aid managerial decision-making.
Ensuring compliance with accounting standards and regulatory mandates during book closures.
Budgeting and Forecasting
Facilitating the budgeting and forecasting processes, encompassing both Group and business unit perspectives.
Engaging in "What-if" scenario planning and variance analysis to preemptively address risks and opportunities.
Presenting financial insights to senior leadership and external stakeholders.
Data Management
Managing and updating financial databases and systems to guarantee data integrity and accuracy.
Identifying potential enhancements in reporting tools and methodologies.
Ad Hoc Analysis
Running ad hoc financial analyses on unit economics, Customer Acquisition Costs (CAC), Lifetime Value (LTV), and headcount KPIs.
Contributing to special projects aimed at driving process improvements and organizational efficiency.
Requirements:
About You
Basic requirements:
2–3 years of experience in FP&A or financial controlling roles.
Proficiency in Excel and familiarity with Business Intelligence tools like Domo, Power BI, Tableau, or Looker.
Strong foundation in accounting principles and procedures.
A Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
Fluency in English and Spanish, with strong communication skills in both.
Demonstrated analytical and quantitative capabilities, coupled with a knack for independent collaboration in fast-paced settings.
Preferred Requirements:
Experience with ERP systems (e.g., Netsuite, SAP) and FP&A software in SaaS platforms.
Exposure to a hi-tech start-up environment.
Ability to communicate complex financial information effectively to non-finance stakeholders through storytelling.

Founded in 2011, the Rover app and website connect dog and cat parents with loving pet sitters and dog walkers in neighborhoods across the US, Canada, and Europe. We empower our community of trusted pet sitters and dog walkers to run their own pet care businesses on Rover with the tools and security of a global company to back them.
Headquartered in Seattle, Washington, we work closely with our teams in Barcelona, San Antonio, Spokane, and remote locations. At Rover, our furry coworkers are just as important as our human ones—and we wouldn’t have it any other way. Along with making the joys of pet parenthood more accessible, we’re committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming community of pet people—and that starts with our employees.
Who We're Looking For
We're looking for a technically-minded Lead Analyst who loves the intersection of Data Modeling and Marketing Strategy. You are someone who isn't satisfied with just "pulling numbers"—you want to understand and architect the underlying logic that makes those numbers true.
In this role, you will be the technical backbone of the Marketing Analytics team. You will take ownership of our reporting infrastructure, driving the transition from legacy reports to clean, automated insights. You will act as the bridge between raw data and advanced Data Science, ensuring our data models are robust enough to support rigorous analytics and experimentation.
You will also serve as the subject matter expert for one of our most complex domains: Attribution. You will navigate our datasets to refine and maintain our logic—helping us distinguish between actions that lead to account creation versus those that drive repeat bookings—ensuring our Lifecycle and Acquisition stakeholders have a reliable view of their impact.
This is a hybrid position that has the minimum expectation to work out of our Barcelona Office in the Poblenou neighborhood two days per week on Mondays and Thursdays. For this reason, candidates must be based in Barcelona or willing to relocate.
Your Impact:
Own Marketing Attribution: Serve as the custodian of our attribution logic. You will maintain and refine our models to ensure the business understands how provider and owner strategies compound to drive New and Repeat bookings, constantly looking for ways to improve our measurement accuracy.
Architect the Reporting Suite: Tackle technical debt head-on by modernizing our reporting infrastructure. You will own the migration of critical business reports to our BI tools, designing clean, SQL-heavy calculations that serve as the "single source of truth" for Lifecycle Marketing and leadership.
Scale Experimentation Operations: Unblock the team on testing by operationalizing our experimentation framework. You will manage the transition to new tools (like Statsig), create SQL templates for test analysis, and conduct code reviews to ensure statistical rigor across the team.
Enable Advanced Analytics: Partner with our Data Scientists to perform Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and build robust data models. By ensuring our data foundation is solid, you will free up the team to focus on high-impact predictive modeling (LTV, Churn) and strategic deep dives.
Your Qualifications:
6+ years of experience in Analytics or Analytics Engineering, with a specific focus on Marketing or Growth data.
Expert-level SQL proficiency. You don't just write queries; you write performant, readable code for complex data modeling, window functions, and heavy calculations within BI tools.
Deep understanding of Marketing Attribution logic. You have experience building, interpreting, or maintaining models that track user journeys across multiple touchpoints (Acquisition vs. Retention/Repeat).
Experience with Data Modeling and creating "Gold Layer" datasets that allow other analysts and stakeholders to self-serve easily.
Strong knowledge of experimentation logic. You understand how to set up data structures to track control vs. variant groups and check for sample ratio mismatches.
Proven ability to manage technical projects from end-to-end, such as migrating reports between tools or auditing tracking setups.
Communication skills that allow you to translate complex data engineering concepts into benefits for non-technical marketing stakeholders.
Nice to Have:
Experience with code-first BI tools (e.g. Mode, Looker, Tableau) where SQL is the primary driver of analysis.
Experience with experimentation platforms like Statsig.
Familiarity with CRM tools (e.g., Iterable), Customer Data Platforms (CDPs), and how their data flows into a warehouse.

As a Credit Risk Decision Analyst, you’ll play a key role in designing credit risk strategies for Satispay products, with a strong focus on BNPL. Your work will include but won’t be limited to quantify credit risk, turn insights into decisions, and help define our risk appetite, while collaborating closely with teammates to deliver data-driven solutions. Here’s what your day-to-day will look like:

Credit risk strategy development
Throughout regular assessment of credit risk performance you will design the risk policy leveraging models, rules, internal and external data, A/B test and any other tool you see fit.
You will eventually recommend approve/decline, limits, and terms; including concise rationales and keeping decisions auditable.
You will be expected to provide the right balance between growth and loss management so the company meets its financial goals.
Cross-product monitoring & quantification
Maintain regular reporting to track credit risk perfomance arises across products (exposure, delinquency, overdue, roll/flow rates, recoveries).
Highlight risk and opportunities and propose actions with expected impact.
You will be collaborating with a large cross functional group including product, marketing, business development etc… to deliver the most optimal value for the company
Risk appetite & policy
Help define target loss ranges and decision thresholds; contribute to policy updates and simple guardrails the business can apply.
Support governance with tidy documentation and on-time reporting.
Data enablement for Finance (Python/SQL)
Use SQL and Python to produce dependable extracts, weekly packs, and lightweight, explainable credit risk reports.
Act as a collaborative internal partner: support ad-hoc data requests that help Finance move faster and make better decisions.
Early-warning & execution hygiene
Set up simple checks/alerts to surface deterioration early.
Ensure exceptions are logged and follow-ups are tracked to closure.
Future scope — Financial Risk Team
As Satispay evolves, this role will become part of the broader Financial Risk team that will model, classify, detect, and identify financial risks end-to-end (today mainly credit; over time expanding to other financial risk areas). You’ll help shape the frameworks, metrics, and tooling that scale with us.
Expect challenges, collaboration, and the freedom to bring your ideas to life. Things change quickly here, so be ready to adapt, take initiative, and shape your role as we grow.
Who we’re looking for
We need a problem-solver who loves teamwork and gets things done. If you're curious and ready for real ownership, you'll fit in! Does this sound like you?
Required experience: 2–5+ years in credit risk policy development (BNPL/short-tenor, SME/consumer, or trade credit).

Technical skills: Working Python (pandas/numpy) and SQL skills to pull/clean data and ship repeatable analyses and reports (this is not a data science role).
Communication skills: Clear, structured communication; short memos, crisp recommendations, and constructive collaboration within Finance and with Product/Data/Ops.
Operating mindset: Organised, documentation-first mindset; decisions and exceptions are review-ready.
Risk ownership: Experience defining or operating risk appetite and simple decision thresholds.

Align product outcomes with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and market opportunities.

Run experiments when uncertainty exists, validating hypotheses before scaling.

Communicate context clearly and proactively to protect focus and align priorities

Wallapop is a Barcelona based scale-up driven by the purpose to empower people to embrace a more conscious and human way of consumption. We believe in a world where collaborative economy is mainstream. This is what drives us.

Powered by technical innovation and continuous improvement, we bring together the scale & trust of classifieds with the marketplace's convenience & reach. Our mission is to enable a connected trade ecosystem, making 2nd-hand the norm through smart use of technology.

The Challenge
As a Growth Product Manager, you'll play a key role in accelerating Wallapop's user growth by owning the strategy and roadmap for acquisition and activation. You'll collaborate with engineers, designers, analysts, and marketing specialists to optimize the user journey from signup to the first 3 successful transactions.
You'll drive product-led growth through data-driven experimentation, improving funnel conversion, and aligning closely with our marketing teams across paid and organic channels.

What You Will Do
Lead the growth strategy for user acquisition and activation across Wallapop's app and web platforms.
Design, run, and analyze experiments to improve engagement at every stage of the journey — from registration to the first transaction.
Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, design, data, and marketing to deliver high-impact growth initiatives.
Partner with the Head of Acquisition to align marketing performance (SEO, SEM, Google Shopping) with in-product experiences that drive long-term activation.
Leverage data and insights to identify and remove friction points in the onboarding and listing/buying flows.
Define and monitor key metrics including activation rate, conversion rate, cost per activated user, and repeat transaction rate.
Cultivate a culture of experimentation, utilizing A/B testing, cohort analysis, and iterative product improvements.
Communicate learnings and results across product, marketing, and leadership teams to ensure shared goals and transparent progress.
What We're Looking For
Experience: Extensive experience in Product Management, with a focus on growth, activation, or conversion optimization.
Experimental Mindset: A proven track record of driving measurable growth through data-informed experimentation and journey optimization.
Analytical Depth: A strong analytical mindset with a comprehensive understanding of growth metrics and lifecycle flows.
Collaborative Leadership: Experience working effectively within cross-functional teams of engineers, data scientists, designers, and marketers.

Technical background or a high degree of comfort collaborating closely with engineering teams on architectural trade-offs.
Understanding of user segmentation, CRM automation, or retention marketing.

Case study Interview - You will present the case study to showcase your product expertise. This usually takes 60 minutes.
Stakeholder Interview - run by relevant stakeholders reflecting the reality of the context of the role, focus on the ability to collaborate & deliver in a cross-functional set-up. This usually takes 60 minutes.

Offer - should you be the right candidate, your offer will be discussed over a call with talent acquisition and will then be confirmed in writing.

Descripción de la empresa

Eurofins Scientific es el líder mundial en ensayos de alimentos, medio ambiente, productos farmacéuticos y cosméticos y en servicios de CRO de agrociencia. También es uno de los líderes mundiales del mercado independiente en servicios de pruebas y laboratorios para genómica, farmacología de descubrimiento, medicina forense, ciencias materiales avanzadas y apoyo a los estudios clínicos.
Con más de 48.000 empleados, en una red de más de 900 empresas independientes, en más de 50 países y operando en más de 800 laboratorios, Eurofins ofrece una cartera de más de 200.000 métodos analíticos para evaluar la seguridad, identidad, composición, autenticidad, origen y pureza de sustancias y productos biológicos, así como para diagnósticos clínicos innovadores

Descripción del empleo

In the context of a fast-growing company, Eurofins is looking for its Net Working Capital (NWC) Champions to join its finance team. Net Working Capital is one of the key financial metrics for the Group and must be improved with on-going and regular actions.
Under the leadership of the NSC Finance Director (FD), the NWC Champion will join the monthly National Business Lines Leaders Committee which will empower her/him to propose, support implementation and monitor all necessary actions to improve the NWC in the different Business Lines in the country.
Committed to NWC improvement in her/his perimeter, she/he will ensure that all best practices are shared and implemented across the different business lines, that the information on NWC, DSO/DPO/DIO, overdue, down payments and other NWC drivers are well, timely and systematically, communicated, analyzed and that systematic actions plans are built, reported, and executed.
Reporting to the NSC Finance Director, to ensure her/his objectives are met: she/he will:
Define action plans with the business leaders to improve the overall cash conversion, participate in the National Business Lines Leaders Committees (NBLLC) to share results and progress and actions plans to improve the NWC on a monthly basis
In particular, she/he will deploy best practices in the below areas:
Trade Accounts Receivables:
Ensure we are signing the right terms with the right clients in all our business lines:
Flag any deviation from our standard GTS 30 days payment terms and propose adjustments as needed
At the request of the National Business Leader and for significant contracts, participate in the proposal and negotiation of the best payment conditions with clients
Set up the Credit Committees and related credit management guidelines per business line, negotiate prepayment for clients with weak credit ratings
Ensure we are invoicing quickly:
Analyze the level of unbilled and work in progress (WIP) revenue, flag any deviation vs Key Guidance Document on Credit Management
Go through the invoicing process to ensure it is efficient, error proof and seamless leading to reduced unbilled and WIP levels,
In case of long-term projects, ensure we are negotiating prepayment and/or milestones payments
Ensure we have the right collection processes in place:
Analyze current collection organization and processes in the different business lines in scope, flag any deviation vs Key Guidance Document on Credit Management
Ensure the Group minimum guidelines in terms of dunning and collection are known and implemented, share good practices, propose improvement as needed
Set clear objectives to significantly reduce overdues for each national business line
Propose actions to the business leaders (such as withholding of analytical reports/goods or order bans/blacklist) in case of systematic late payments from clients and/or default (bankruptcy, bad credit rating etc.)
Trade Accounts Payables:
Monitor DPO evolution and improvements in close relation with the Purchasing organization and the Business leaders as needed, flag any deviation vs the Key Guidance Document on PTP
Ensure we are signing right terms with the right suppliers: propose the best payment terms possible, ensure the policy is then systematically implemented
Ensure we reduce to the strict minimum any prepayment to suppliers (including yearly payments, subscriptions etc.)
Other Net Working Capital components:
Monitor Inventory level and DIO, communicate proactively with business leaders showing the highest level and/or the biggest increases. Evaluate and propose, in relation with Purchasing Teams, alternative to large deliveries, securing procurement without additional inventories, etc...
Employees related liabilities and other receivables and payables: monitor and forecast the evolutions of these drivers
Participate in the budget and forecast processes for Net Working Capital by supporting the National Business Lines to set up ambitious targets for their teams,
Ensure the selected KPIs supporting the actions plans are well known, reported, analyzed, and communicated to the right stakeholders in scope (DSO reports, DPO reports, overdue, aging reports etc.)
Produce regular reports and proactively alert management on deviations. This includes:
Weekly qualitative exchanges with Business leaders, Global treasury & Finance Director
Direct contact with Top Management to alert about deviation/ lack of progress

Requisitos
Bachelor degree in Finance or Economics.
A successful prior working experience (5-7 years) is mandatory, gained preferably in credit management.
Experience as Financial Controller, Financial Analyst, Treasury Manager or in Audit could be considered.
Good knowledge of accounting principles and understanding of business and accounting/reporting processes (P2P, O2C)
Daring and bold, able to push her/his ideas and challenge opposition.
Strong analytical & communication skills (ability to analyze and summarize big volumes of data and to articulate ideas in a clear and concise manner)
Accuracy of work, pays attention to details, like numbers; Good organizational skills.
English fluency to report and communicate beyond perimeter (within the NWC Community etc.) is required.

Hybrid model with possibility of work-from-home, when the candidate has consolidate her/his position.
Flexible benefits package.
Permanent contract.
